programme: DLX5 and NKX3-2 are homeodomain drivers of a BMP-RUNX2 chondro-osteogenic differentiation programme: their target lists directly overlap on RUNX2, BMP4 and COL10A1, and DLX5 alone carries the rest of the canonical osteoblast/chondrocyte output (BMP2, COL1A1, SPP1, ALPL, IBSP, WNT10B, DKK1). HOXA11 sits alongside it supplying matrix-remodeling components of the same connective-tissue axis (COL3A1, MMP2, plus its paralog HOXA10). GLI1's own target set (DKK2, DKK3, SFRP1 — Wnt antagonists) is the expected Hedgehog partner of BMP-driven mesenchymal reprogramming, tying it into the same module rather than standing apart from it.
role_in_a: In cardiovascular disease this exact gene set (RUNX2, BMP2, SPP1, ALPL, IBSP, COL1A1) is the standard signature of osteogenic transdifferentiation of vascular smooth-muscle and valve interstitial cells — the mechanism underlying vascular and valvular calcification.
role_in_b: In the gut, BMP and Hedgehog signalling from GLI1+ subepithelial/stromal cells normally patterns the crypt-villus axis and epithelial stem-cell niche; a specific, established role for this programme in IBS itself is not part of current disease understanding — visceral hypersensitivity and motility are the recognized IBS mechanisms, not stromal osteo-chondrogenic reprogramming.
shared_axis: If this module is active in both tissues, the plausible bridge is that DLX5/NKX3-2/GLI1-driven BMP output is a general mesenchymal/stromal reprogramming circuit that vascular cells co-opt toward calcification and gut stromal cells co-opt toward niche or fibrotic remodeling — the same wiring, different tissue context and end phenotype.
reasoning: The module is genuinely nameable from the data itself (RUNX2/BMP4/COL10A1 shared between DLX5 and NKX3-2's own target lists, not an outside claim), and its role in vascular calcification in CVD is well established biology. But nothing here documents this programme as a mechanism in IBS specifically, Open Targets shows no association for three of the four carrying factors in either disease, and the one hit (GLI1-IBS) is a low percentile with an ambiguous paper — so the account rests on reasoning about shared stromal signalling logic rather than on retrieved evidence for this pair.
support: 30802137 — retrieved for GLI1 and IBS, but reports ANO1 regulation in intestinal tissue rather than a GLI1-IBS disease link directly; relevance uncertain. No PMIDs were retrieved for DLX5, NKX3-2, or HOXA11 with either disease.
how_to_falsify: Knock down DLX5 and NKX3-2 in vascular smooth-muscle or valve interstitial cells from CVD patients under calcifying conditions — if RUNX2/BMP4/COL10A1/SPP1 induction is unaffected, the module is not TF-dependent in this tissue. Separately, compare BMP4/RUNX2-target expression in GLI1+ colonic subepithelial cells between IBS patients and controls — no shift would argue against any functional role of this programme in IBS.
caveats: RUNX2, the node both DLX5 and NKX3-2 converge on, does not itself appear among the survivors — it was removed as tissue-generic (percentile 0.921) and had already fallen out at 0.47 recurrence, so its absence reflects the filtering, not irrelevance to the mechanism. Recurrence among the four carrying factors spans a wide range, from DLX5 at 31/32 down to HOXA11 and GLI1 at 16/32 — the DLX5/NKX3-2 core is far better supported than the HOXA11/GLI1 additions. Blood and colorectal tissue are only weakly connected anatomically for this specific axis, and only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 32 comparisons. The other eight survivors (HOXC9, ZBTB4, BCL11A, HOPX, TCF3, CUX1, SNAI1, TGFB1I1) span unrelated lineage programmes (erythroid, B-lymphoid, EMT) and were deliberately left out of this account rather than forced into one story — the record overall is sparse and uncertain for every factor here, and this should be read as a low-confidence lead, not a settled mechanism.
